summary: Gemma 4 is introduced as a family of open-source models released under Apache 2.0 licensing, comprising four sizes. The two smaller 'effective' models (2B and 4B) target on-device deployment on phones, tablets, and laptops, while the two larger models—a 26B mixture-of-experts and a 31B dense model—target advanced reasoning and agentic workflows. The 31B dense model ranked third on the global AI leaderboard, outperforming models 20x its size, and features a 256K context length with native support for thinking, function calling, and structured JSON outputs. The 26B MoE uses only 3.8B active parameters per forward pass, selecting 8 of 128 total experts plus a shared router expert that is 3x the size of regular experts. Architectural improvements include a 5:1 ratio of interleaved local-to-global attention layers (4:1 for the 2B), with sliding windows of 512 tokens for smaller models and 1024 for larger ones. Grouped query attention groups 2 queries per key-value head in local layers and 8 in global layers, with global KV head length doubled to 512 versus 256 in local layers. The effective models use Per Layer Embeddings (PLE), storing a dedicated 256-dimension embedding table per layer in flash memory rather than VRAM, significantly reducing on-device memory constraints. E2B has 2.3B effective parameters with 5.1B representational depth across 35 layers, while E4B has 42 layers. Multimodal support is native across all models, with vision encoders of 550M parameters for larger models and 150M for effective models. Variable aspect ratios and resolutions (five options) allow developers to control image token budgets—a major improvement over Gemma 3's pan-and-scan approach. Images are split into 16x16 pixel patches, grouped into 3x3 grids to form single embeddings, yielding N/9 soft tokens that are linearly projected to the model. A 280-token budget corresponds to 2,520 patches, with 560 and 1120 token budgets available for high-resolution OCR and object detection tasks. Audio support in E2B and E4B uses a 305M parameter conformer encoder processing embeddings rather than tokens, paired with an audio tokenizer that converts raw audio through a mel spectrogram, downsamples via two convolutional layers, and outputs N/4 soft tokens into the conformer. Getting started options include self-hosting via Hugging Face, Kaggle, and Ollama, or cloud deployment through AI Studio and Vertex AI for the larger models.

takeaways: Gemma 4 ships in four sizes: effective 2B and 4B for on-device use, plus a 26B MoE and 31B dense for advanced reasoning.
Variable aspect ratios and resolutions let developers control token budgets per image, replacing Gemma 3's pan-and-scan with single-pass processing of varying patch counts.
Vision patches are grouped into 3x3 grids to form single embeddings, producing N/9 soft tokens linearly projected to the model; a 280-token budget yields 2,520 patches.
Audio support in E2B and E4B uses a 305M parameter conformer plus an audio tokenizer with mel spectrogram and two convolutional downsampling layers, outputting N/4 soft tokens.
The 26B MoE activates only 3.8B parameters per forward pass using 8 of 128 experts plus a shared router expert 3x the size of regular experts.
Interleaved local/global attention (5:1 ratio, or 4:1 for 2B) with sliding windows and grouped query attention reduce computational cost while preserving information flow.
Per Layer Embeddings store per-layer 256-dimension tables in flash memory instead of VRAM, enabling on-device deployment under tight memory constraints.
Models are available via self-hosting (Hugging Face, Kaggle, Ollama) or cloud deployment (AI Studio, Vertex AI) for larger models.

sections.title: Introduction to Gemma 4 and Model Sizes
sections.summary: Cassidy introduces Gemma 4 as the latest open-source model family with four sizes: two effective on-device models (2B, 4B) and two larger models (26B MoE, 31B dense). The 26B MoE is Gemma's first mixture-of-experts model with 3.9B active parameters. Both large models ranked in the top six on LM arena.

sections.title: Apache 2.0 Licensing and Model Capabilities
sections.summary: Gemma 4 moves to Apache 2.0 licensing for developer accessibility. The 31B dense is a multimodal model built for advanced reasoning, ranked #3 globally, with 256K context length and native support for thinking, function calling, and structured JSON. The 26B MoE uses 3.8B active params with 128 experts and 8 activated per pass.

sections.title: Architecture: Interleaved Local/Global Attention
sections.summary: Gemma 4 introduces interleaved local and global attention layers at a 5:1 ratio (4:1 for the 2B model). Local layers use sliding windows of 512 (small) or 1024 (large) tokens; global layers attend to all preceding tokens. The last layer is always global. Grouped query attention groups 2 queries per KV head locally and 8 globally, with global KV head length doubled to 512.

sections.title: MoE Architecture Details
sections.summary: The MoE replaces the standard feedforward network with 128 total experts and 8 activated per forward pass, plus a shared router expert activated every pass that is 3x the size of regular experts.

sections.title: Effective Models and Per Layer Embeddings (PLE)
sections.summary: Effective models distinguish operational from representational parameters (E2B: 2.3B effective, 5.1B representational). PLE adds a per-layer embedding table (256-dimension) stored in flash memory instead of VRAM, addressing the primary on-device memory constraint. Each token gets an embedding at every layer, projected up to full embedding size at decoder block end. E2B has 35 layers, E4B has 42.

sections.title: Multimodal Vision Encoder Advances
sections.summary: Gemma 4 is natively multimodal, building on Gemma 3's vision and Gemma 3N's audio/vision/text. Vision encoders are 550M parameters for large models and 150M for effective models. Variable aspect ratios and resolutions (five options) let developers control soft token budgets. Images are split into 16x16 pixel patches, flattened, projected to embeddings, and positionally encoded, with spatial positional encoding critical for varying aspect ratios.

sections.title: Variable Resolution and Patch Processing Pipeline
sections.summary: Variable resolution lets developers select token budgets per image, critical for OCR and spatial object recognition (560/1120 token budgets for high quality) versus text-only use cases with smaller budgets. This replaces Gemma 3's pan-and-scan, which split variable-resolution images into multiple padded square sub-images processed sequentially. Patches are grouped into 3x3 grids to form single embeddings, yielding N/9 soft tokens linearly projected to the model. A 280-token budget corresponds to 2,520 patches.

sections.title: Audio Processing Architecture
sections.summary: Audio support is added to E2B and E4B for translation and speech recognition via a 305M parameter conformer audio encoder processing embeddings rather than tokens, combined with an audio tokenizer. Raw audio passes through a mel spectrogram, split into N mel chunks, downsampled through two convolutional layers to produce N/4 soft tokens fed into the conformer. The conformer follows a similar architecture to dense and MoE models but adds a convolutional layer.

sections.title: Getting Started with Gemma 4
sections.summary: Gemma 4 models can be self-hosted via Hugging Face, Kaggle, and Ollama, or accessed through cloud-hosted options on AI Studio and Vertex AI for the larger 31B and 26B models, enabling immediate prototyping of agentic workflows and function calling.
